title: Inspect list.am listings and define the source mapping
goal: Analyze Yerevan long-term apartment listings and map available source fields to the shared data contract.
criteria: Document available fields, missing values, pagination, and source update behavior.
Provide a small sanitized or synthetic parser fixture and field mapping.
Document collection constraints, rate limits, and a reproducible fallback import if access fails.

title: Implement the PostgreSQL/PostGIS schema and migrations
goal: Design and implement storage for properties, listings, observations, infrastructure, estimates, signals, reviews, and ingestion runs.
criteria: Publish an ER diagram and Alembic migrations that work on an empty database.
Preserve source identity and price history with suitable constraints and geographic indexes.
Provide synthetic seed data and coordinate schema ownership with backend.

title: Build the listing collection and normalization pipeline
goal: Collect the selected list.am segment and normalize records for the Yerevan rental market.
criteria: Provide a repeatable CLI with bounded retries, pagination, and run summaries.
Normalize monthly USD amounts while preserving original currencies, conversion provenance, and utility-cost uncertainty.
Quarantine invalid records and test representative parsing and normalization failures.

title: Handle duplicates, observations, and listing lifecycle
goal: Make repeated collection safe and keep inactive inventory distinguishable from collection failures.
criteria: Repeated runs do not duplicate listings or observations; price changes remain traceable.
Document and verify duplicate grouping without merging unrelated properties.
Deactivate records only after successful source observations under a documented staleness policy.

title: Add Yerevan districts and infrastructure proximity features
goal: Enrich listings with districts, coordinates, and distances to metro stations, universities, and a defined city-center reference.
criteria: Record geographic data provenance and coordinate confidence; flag unresolved locations.
Produce distance features with explicit units and a documented center definition.
Validate known location examples and make the features available to ML and API consumers.

title: Publish reproducible training and evaluation datasets
goal: Export versioned datasets following the feature contract and leakage-prevention rules.
criteria: Export includes observation dates, duplicate groups, feature definitions, and provenance.
Provide a data-quality report covering missingness, invalid values, duplicates, and neighborhood coverage.
Demonstrate reproducible snapshot generation without committing raw listings or personal data.

title: Build neighborhood asking-price index aggregates
goal: Produce weekly neighborhood asking-price statistics for comparable active inventory.
criteria: Provide median USD/month and USD/m², sample counts, period, and data freshness.
Define sparse-neighborhood behavior and avoid presenting listing prices as signed-contract prices.
Validate aggregates against a small known dataset and expose a stable query interface to backend.

title: Validate ingestion recovery and deliver the data runbook
goal: Verify production ingestion behavior and make collection reproducible for teammates.
criteria: Demonstrate initial load, repeated load, price change, and recovery from a failed run.
Verify failed collection does not clear active inventory and incomplete records stay traceable.
Deliver source limitations, rerun instructions, and a reproducible demo dataset for the final demo.

title: Model the municipal real estate ontology
goal: Define the ontology for properties, listings, districts, infrastructure, estimates, and risk evidence.
criteria: Commit an OWL/RDF ontology and a readable class/relationship diagram.
Provide competency questions and examples covering Yerevan locations and property characteristics.
Demonstrate consistency and sample queries/inferences with Protégé or RDFLib.

title: Define the feature and evaluation contract
goal: Agree with data and backend owners on model inputs, outputs, and evaluation methodology.
criteria: Define feature types, missing-value behavior, units, and prediction response structure.
Specify chronological splits and duplicate-group isolation to prevent leakage.
Define baseline, error metrics, interval coverage/width, and neighborhood-level evaluation.

title: Implement the comparable-property median baseline
goal: Create an explainable valuation baseline using comparable rental listings.
criteria: Return expected monthly USD rent, comparable count, and selection explanation.
Handle sparse comparables with a documented fallback or insufficient_data result.
Provide a callable interface and deterministic checks on controlled examples for backend integration.

title: Train and compare the rental price model
goal: Train a CatBoost regressor and compare it fairly with the baseline.
criteria: Run a reproducible experiment on the agreed split and report baseline/model MAE and median absolute error.
Report neighborhood results and investigate large errors and data leakage.
Save preprocessing, feature schema, model artifact, and version metadata; keep the baseline fallback if ML is worse.

title: Calibrate prediction intervals and valuation confidence
goal: Add empirically evaluated rental price intervals and defensible abstention behavior.
criteria: Calibrate intervals without using test labels and report held-out coverage and width.
Implement within_range, above_range, below_range, and insufficient_data consistently.
Evaluate sparse, missing-feature, and out-of-distribution examples; explain confidence limitations.

title: Implement ontology rules and valuation explanations
goal: Connect geographic facts and property descriptions to traceable inference and readable explanations.
criteria: Implement versioned rules with evidence for proximity and description/location inconsistencies.
Show at least three representative inference examples, including a missing-data case.
Separate inferred facts from learned price effects and supply structured explanations to backend.

title: Package the inference interface for backend integration
goal: Deliver a versioned prediction package usable by the FastAPI application.
criteria: Provide one documented inference entry point matching the shared contract.
Include model/rule versions, data freshness, interval, factors, and fallback behavior.
Verify artifact loading and predictions in the backend container with a reproducible example.

title: Deliver model and ontology evaluation evidence
goal: Prepare evidence for the final defense and document practical limitations.
criteria: Publish a model card, reproducible evaluation commands, and comparison charts.
Show ontology competency-question results and rule validation examples.
Evaluate risk-related examples separately from price errors; state limitations without claiming unmeasured fraud accuracy.

title: Finalize shared data, API, and integration contracts
goal: Coordinate the contracts used by all four components before parallel implementation.
criteria: Publish OpenAPI schemas for listings, coordinate valuations with standard deviations, estimates, market indexes, and reviews, including validation, pagination, and errors.
Agree units, USD conversion semantics, nullable fields, identifiers, and model inputs with the owners.
Provide synthetic request/response fixtures so frontend and ML can work independently.

title: Bootstrap FastAPI and the local Docker environment
goal: Create a runnable backend and shared local environment.
criteria: Docker Compose starts the API and PostgreSQL/PostGIS with documented setup.
Provide health checks, environment examples, database configuration, and a model stub.
Verify a clean setup and basic API behavior without external credentials.

title: Implement listing search, details, and geographic APIs
goal: Serve normalized listing data through the agreed API.
criteria: Implement district/price/rooms/area filters, stable pagination, details, and bounded map queries.
Return source links, freshness, missing-data states, and inactive status consistently.
Verify query validation, no-result cases, and representative database-backed responses.

title: Integrate valuation and ontology results
goal: Expose baseline valuation first and support the versioned ML package when available.
criteria: Expose expected USD rent, interval when available, factors, versions, and insufficient-data behavior.
Persist estimates with freshness/version metadata and avoid silently returning stale results.
Integrate the baseline for MVP, then B07 for final delivery; verify success and model-failure paths.

title: Implement risk signals and the protected review workflow
goal: Create explainable risk rules and a reviewer-only queue with recorded decisions.
criteria: Keep price anomalies separate from fraud-risk evidence; version rules and prevent duplicate signals.
Implement queue filters, status changes, decision reasons, and audit timestamps.
Protect reviewer endpoints with authentication/authorization and verify unauthorized requests are rejected.

title: Expose market analytics and data freshness
goal: Provide frontend-ready neighborhood and trend endpoints.
criteria: Return periods, USD units, sample counts, and source freshness with every aggregate.
Handle sparse data and empty periods without fabricated values.
Verify API responses against data-layer aggregates and the agreed chart fixtures.

title: Add pull-request checks and container build workflows
goal: Create CI for meaningful component checks and reproducible container builds.
criteria: Run backend/data/ML checks and frontend type/build checks as components become available.
Build required Docker images and document version/tag conventions.
Verify a failing check is reported and configure PR review/protection where supported by the repository plan.

title: Provision and deploy the AWS application with Terraform
goal: Deploy the application using the agreed AWS architecture.
criteria: Terraform defines frontend S3/CloudFront, backend ECS/ECR, RDS/PostGIS, artifact storage, networking, and logging.
Configure HTTPS, appropriate CORS, private database access, and secrets handling; record cost assumptions before provisioning.
Deploy versioned images/frontend builds and document migrations, rollback, and teardown; do not place credentials in Git.

title: Configure weekly cron ingestion and operational monitoring
goal: Run ingestion on schedule and make failures visible.
criteria: Configure an explicit weekly cron expression in Terraform for EventBridge Scheduler (initial schedule: Sunday 03:00, Asia/Yerevan) to launch the collection ECS task with overlap prevention; make the schedule configurable.
Record run status, retries, and freshness; add failure visibility through CloudWatch.
Demonstrate a manual run, a failed run, and recovery without clearing inventory; document rerun steps.

title: Complete end-to-end release verification and the demo runbook
goal: Coordinate final integration and produce a reproducible release demonstration.
criteria: Verify collection → database → valuation → signals → API → UI → reviewer decision using real and controlled examples.
Record resolved integration defects, deployed version, smoke checks, and known limitations.
Deliver setup/deployment/demo instructions with a baseline-vs-ML example and rollback procedure.

title: Design the user journeys and screen contracts
goal: Define the catalogue, detail, analytics, and reviewer journeys before implementation.
criteria: Provide lightweight wireframes and a shared UI structure for desktop and mobile.
Define loading, empty, error, insufficient-data, and stale-data states.
Review required API data with backend and align labels so risk signals are not presented as fraud verdicts.

title: Bootstrap React/TypeScript and a mock API layer
goal: Create the frontend shell and a mock-backed integration boundary.
criteria: Vite app runs with routing, reusable layout, and environment-based API configuration.
Use shared synthetic fixtures behind a typed API client.
Provide type/build checks and demonstrate switching between mock and real API modes.

title: Build the listing catalogue and filters
goal: Implement browsing of Yerevan rentals with useful comparisons.
criteria: Display monthly USD rent, area, rooms, district, and source freshness.
Implement filters and pagination with URL state and clear/reset behavior.
Verify loading, empty, error, and missing-field cases; integrate C03 when available.

title: Build listing details and the valuation explanation view
goal: Show the requested rent alongside the estimated range and explanation.
criteria: Display expected price, interval when available, comparables, factors, versions/freshness, and original source link.
Separate price status from risk signals and handle insufficient_data without invented scores.
Use responsive layout and connect the real C04 endpoint when ready.

title: Implement the interactive property and infrastructure map
goal: Make the viewport-filling map the opening Browse experience and connect map exploration to the listing catalogue.
criteria: Render geolocated listings, selected property details, and relevant infrastructure with MapLibre GL JS.
Keep filters and map selection consistent and handle missing coordinates.
Document map/tile attribution and verify marker behavior and bounded-query performance on representative data.
Open Browse with a viewport-filling map below the header and compact floating or collapsible filters; preserve an accessible list alternative and usable mobile layout.
Provide 2D/3D switching with building extrusions where verified Yerevan footprint/height data is available; document coverage and provide a 2D fallback without invented heights.

Define the colored rental layer with units, legend, sample counts and freshness; keep insufficient-data areas neutral. Real aggregate integration requires A07/C06, and any synthetic preview must be labeled.

title: Build neighborhood market analytics
goal: Visualize neighborhood asking-price indexes and trends with Recharts.
criteria: Provide neighborhood/time controls and clearly labeled USD/month and USD/m² measures.
Show observation counts, periods, and freshness; distinguish missing data from zero.
Verify rendered values against API fixtures and real aggregate responses.

title: Build the authenticated reviewer interface
goal: Enable authorized reviewers to inspect signals and record decisions.
criteria: Provide login/session handling, queue filters, evidence details, and review actions.
Require a decision reason and show saved status/history without duplicate submissions.
Handle expired/unauthorized sessions and connect the protected backend workflow.

title: Validate the integrated UI and prepare the frontend demo
goal: Verify the complete frontend against the deployed application.
criteria: Add meaningful Playwright coverage for browsing, filters, valuation, analytics, and reviewer decisions.
Check mobile layout, keyboard navigation, empty/error/stale states, and production API configuration.
Resolve UI integration defects and deliver a short demo sequence with screenshots and known limitations.

title: Build the coordinate-based price statistics and assessment pipeline
goal: Implement the required Python analysis pipeline using Pandas and Scikit-Learn to assess rental prices around supplied coordinates.
criteria: Define radius/time/property comparability rules, duplicate handling, and minimum sample size with the data owner.
Return count, mean, sample standard deviation (n−1) in USD/month and USD/m² where available, cohort metadata, and a valuation assessment; distinguish observed dispersion from prediction intervals.
Support coordinate-only neighborhood reference and property-specific valuation when enough inputs exist; verify sparse, out-of-coverage, and known synthetic samples without fabricating values.

title: Expose the coordinate valuation and price standard deviation REST endpoint
goal: Implement POST /api/v1/valuations for supplied coordinates, optional property features, local dispersion, and valuation assessments.
criteria: Validate coordinate bounds, Yerevan coverage, supported radius, and property inputs; document request/response examples in OpenAPI.
Integrate B09 and return cohort size, units, mean, standard deviations, valuation assessment, freshness, and model/rule versions; clearly label coordinate-only results as area references.
Verify controlled-sample numeric results, insufficient-data/null behavior, invalid inputs, and an end-to-end coordinate request through the deployed API.

title: Add coordinate-based valuation lookup and price dispersion results
goal: Let users request an assessment for a coordinate pair or map selection and inspect local price dispersion.
criteria: Provide validated coordinate input or map selection and optional property characteristics connected to POST /api/v1/valuations.
Display the assessment, comparable count, search radius/time window, freshness, and standard deviations with explicit USD/month and USD/m² units.
Explain that standard deviation is observed market dispersion, keep it separate from prediction intervals, and handle insufficient data, unsupported locations, and request errors.

title: Inventory information assets and assess application security risks
goal: Identify FairRent information assets, trust boundaries and security risks, and agree proportionate controls with component owners.
criteria: Document asset ownership and classification for listing data, reviewer identities, credentials, model artifacts and logs; assess confidentiality, integrity and availability needs.
Create a data-flow diagram and STRIDE threat model; record likelihood, impact, controls, residual risk and remediation owners in a prioritized risk register.
Map selected controls to NIST CSF or CIS Controls and document access, secret-handling and incident-reporting procedures; do not claim framework certification.

title: Add security checks and remediate dependency and container findings
goal: Integrate actionable secret, dependency and container security checks into the existing delivery workflow with the CI owner.
criteria: Add secret and dependency checks and container-image scanning where supported; verify detection using harmless synthetic fixtures and document severity handling and time-limited exceptions.
Review workflow token permissions, untrusted PR inputs, action references and artifact access with Artyom; document fixes without introducing cloud credentials into CI.
Review container runtime privileges, unnecessary packages and exposed ports; fix verified findings and record retest evidence.

title: Verify application authorization and untrusted input handling
goal: Verify reviewer access controls, frontend sessions and safe handling of untrusted listing and request data.
criteria: Add tests for missing, expired and invalid tokens, incorrect reviewer role, object access, forbidden review updates and concurrency conflicts; distinguish application roles from AWS IAM.
Verify listing text rendering, external links, session/token handling, query parameterization and safe errors; test representative XSS and injection inputs against owned test environments.
Verify pagination, bounded geographic queries, request-size/time limits and URL-fetching restrictions where applicable; coordinate implementation fixes and retest with component owners.

title: Verify transport security and data and model artifact integrity
goal: Verify protected transport, data handling and model artifact integrity in the deployed application with infrastructure and data owners.
criteria: Inspect the deployed HTTPS certificate chain, hostname and validity using OpenSSL or equivalent tools; verify HTTP-to-HTTPS behavior and absence of mixed content, reporting AWS configuration changes to Artyom.
Verify dataset and model artifact checksums against a trusted manifest and demonstrate rejection of a modified artifact; distinguish integrity hashes from authentication or digital signatures.
Review application database privileges, sensitive log fields, data exports and reachable service boundaries; verify agreed protections without changing AWS resources, IAM or cloud permissions.

title: Complete security verification and the incident response runbook
goal: Verify security fixes before release and make application incident handling reproducible for the team.
criteria: Perform scoped manual and automated security checks against owned staging services; record reproduction, impact, fix and retest results, with explicit owner acceptance for unresolved release risks.
Document detection, triage, containment, recovery, evidence handling and post-incident review; rehearse a simulated unauthorized reviewer action or synthetic credential-exposure scenario.
Verify audit events identify actor, action, outcome and UTC time without tokens or sensitive payloads; summarize findings and residual risks for the release demo.

title: Configure the Linux environment and secure access
goal: Optional after the core release and security work, only if time remains. Configure a Linux environment for the Compose application and document access, networking and storage.
criteria: Document VM OS/resources, a non-root administrator, SSH key access, file permissions and firewall rules; verify access before restricting SSH.
Start the API and PostGIS from the repository instructions, verify health/readiness, and document container networking and persistent storage.
Keep secrets and real listing data out of Git; provide a reproducible setup and teardown guide with sanitized command output.

title: Document service monitoring and Linux troubleshooting
goal: Optional after the core release and security work, only if time remains. Implement service monitoring and document application and host diagnostics.
criteria: Document checks for API health/readiness, Compose status/logs, listening ports, disk space, memory and host services.
Provide a small shell check script with meaningful exit codes and no credentials in output; demonstrate healthy and unavailable database states.
Document log locations, bounded log retention and a symptom-to-diagnosis checklist with sanitized evidence.

title: Implement and verify database backup and restore
goal: Optional after the core release and security work, only if time remains. Implement reproducible PostgreSQL/PostGIS backup and restore procedures and verify recovery using synthetic data.
criteria: Provide documented pg_dump/pg_restore commands or shell scripts, backup naming, restricted permissions and a retention policy; exclude backups from Git.
Restore into a separate disposable database or Compose project and verify synthetic rows and PostGIS functionality without overwriting the working database.
Record backup/restore duration, database and PostGIS versions, failure handling and rerun steps; document how the procedure relates to production RDS backups.

title: Validate service recovery and deliver the operations runbook
goal: Optional after the core release and security work, only if time remains. Verify application recovery from service failures and deliver reproducible operating procedures.
criteria: Reproduce database unavailability, an occupied API port and invalid configuration in a controlled environment; record symptoms, diagnosis and recovery.
Demonstrate recovery after VM reboot and a database restore drill; verify health/readiness and retained synthetic data.
Publish a runbook covering access, startup/shutdown, logs, backup/restore, recovery and environment teardown; have another teammate reproduce one procedure.
